bottom_line: In men with hypercholesterolemia and no history of myocardial infarction, pravastatin vs placebo reduced the risk of definite nonfatal MI or death from CHD by 31% (95% CI, 17 to 43 percent; P<0.001).
implications: These data support that, over 4.9 years of follow-up, pravastatin reduced definite nonfatal MI or death from CHD (31% risk reduction; absolute 5-year risks 7.9% vs 5.5%) and reduced death from all cardiovascular causes (32% risk reduction), while showing no statistically significant difference in death from noncardiovascular causes (P=0.54) or incident cancer (P=0.55); the all-cause mortality reduction did not reach conventional statistical significance in this report (P=0.051; 95% CI 0 to 40).

major_points.text: Primary end point was first event of nonfatal myocardial infarction or death from coronary heart disease (combined).
major_points.quote: the primary end point of the study was the occurrence of nonfatal myocardial infarction or death from coronary heart disease as a ﬁrst event; these two categories were combined.

major_points.text: No excess of noncardiovascular deaths was observed with pravastatin compared with placebo.
major_points.quote: There were 56 deaths from noncardiovascular causes in the pravastatin group and 62 in the placebo group (P=0.54).

major_points.text: Death from all cardiovascular causes was reduced (73 vs 50; P=0.033; risk reduction 32% [3 to 53]).
major_points.quote: Death from all cardiovascular causes                  73 (2.3)           50 (1.6)   0.033       32 (3 to 53)

major_points.text: All-cause mortality showed a 22% relative reduction (P=0.051; 95% CI 0 to 40).

guidelines_referenced.text: National Cholesterol Education Program (NCEP) Adult Treatment Panel II
guidelines_referenced.quote: Summary of the second report of the National Cholesterol Education Program (NCEP) expert panel on detection, evaluation, and treatment of high blood cholesterol in adults (Adult Treatment Panel II).

guidelines_referenced.text: EAS Task Force for Prevention of Coronary Heart Disease
guidelines_referenced.quote: EAS Task Force for Prevention of Coronary Heart Disease. Prevention of coronary heart disease: scientiﬁc background and new clinical guidelines.

guidelines_referenced.text: American Heart Association and the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
guidelines_referenced.quote: The cholesterol facts: a summary of the evidence relating dietary fats, serum cholesterol, and coronary heart disease: a joint statement by the American Heart Association and the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

inclusion_criteria.quote: men with hypercholesterolemia and no history of myocardial infarction

inclusion_criteria.text: Nonfasting plasma cholesterol level at least 252 mg/dl at first visit (with no history of myocardial infarction).
inclusion_criteria.quote: those whose nonfasting plasma cholesterol level was at least 252 mg per deciliter (6.5 mmol per liter) but who had no history of myocardial infarction

inclusion_criteria.text: Fasting LDL cholesterol at least 155 mg/dl at second visit to continue screening.
inclusion_criteria.quote: If on this occasion the LDL cholesterol level was at least 155 mg per deciliter (4.0 mmol per liter)

inclusion_criteria.text: At randomization: fasting LDL cholesterol at least 155 mg/dl during the second and third visits, with at least one value ≥174 mg/dl and one value ≤232 mg/dl.
inclusion_criteria.quote: fasting LDL cholesterol level of at least 155 mg per deciliter during the second and third visits, with at least one value of 174 mg per deciliter or above (4.5 mmol per liter) and one value of 232 mg per deciliter or below (6.0 mmol per liter)

exclusion_criteria.text: Serious ECG abnormalities per Minnesota code 1, 4-1, 5-1, or 7-1-1.
exclusion_criteria.quote: no serious ECG abnormalities according to Minnesota code18 1 (pathologic Q waves), 4-1, 5-1, or 7-1-1
or arrhythmia such as atrial ﬁbrillation

exclusion_criteria.text: History of myocardial infarction or other serious illness.
exclusion_criteria.quote: and no history of myocardial infarction or other serious illness

baseline.characteristic: Smoking status, Current smoker — no. of subjects (%)

criticisms.text: For death from coronary heart disease, definite-only analysis was not significant, probably because of smaller number of events.
criticisms.quote: but not in the analysis of deﬁnite cases alone, probably because of the smaller number of events in this group.

criticisms.text: Subgroups with multiple risk factors or vascular disease were too small to show a statistically significant effect.
criticisms.quote: The numbers of subjects in the subgroups with either multiple risk factors at base line or vascular disease at base line were too small to show a statistically signiﬁcant effect.

criticisms.text: Plasma cholesterol level was not a significant factor, mainly due to narrow range used for study entry.
criticisms.quote: The plasma cholesterol level was not a signiﬁcant factor, principally because of the narrow range of cholesterol values used as a criterion for entry into the study.
